title: Negative selection — clearing out the bad apples from the T-cell repertoire
note: Supports thymic negative selection as a mechanism contributing to removal of strongly self-reactive T-cell clones.

title: Positive and negative selection of T cells
note: Supports repertoire selection and tolerance framing; agent mapping remains hypothetical.

title: Clonal expansion of innate and adaptive lymphocytes
note: Supports proliferation of responsive lymphocyte clones and subsequent differentiation into multiple fates.

title: Innate Immunological Memory: From Plants to Animals
note: Used conservatively to ground immune-memory concepts; software memory-compaction mapping is a hypothesis.

title: Complement - a key system for immune surveillance and homeostasis
note: Supports complement as a tightly connected recognition, amplification, effector, and regulatory network.

title: Overview of Complement Activation and Regulation
note: Supports strong regulation of complement activation to limit injury to host tissue.

title: Danger signals – damaged-self recognition across the tree of life
note: Supports use of pathogen-associated and damage-associated signals in innate immune activation; exact danger-model interpretations remain debated and should not be overstated.

title: The regulation and differentiation of regulatory T cells and their dysfunction in autoimmune diseases
note: Supports central role of regulatory T cells in regulating immune responses and self-tolerance.

title: How regulatory T cells work
note: Supports multiple active suppressive mechanisms; software negative-signal mapping is hypothetical.

title: Antigen presentation by dendritic cells and their instruction of CD4+ T helper cell responses
note: Supports antigen presentation, co-stimulatory signaling, and context-dependent instruction of T-cell responses.

title: The interaction of innate immune and adaptive immune system
note: Supports substantial innate-adaptive crosstalk; the Atlas abstracts this as a fast/slow escalation hypothesis rather than claiming exact equivalence.
